title: a completed run sealed as "in flight" once, and was not reproduced
body:
# 0015: a completed run sealed as "in flight" once, and was not reproduced

## Tags

seals, verdict, race, observation, not-reproduced, prolix

## Summary

`bin/prolix test mix` completed normally and its verdict file said the run had not completed.

The `.out` log ended with `Result: 746 passed (19 doctests, 727 tests)` and the ExUnit dot line above it. The matching `.errors` seal held the in-flight sentinel:

    run in flight (or aborted before sealing) -- no completed verdict; see the .out log

An immediate re-run of the same command sealed correctly: 0 bytes, exit 0, same 746.

**Observed once. The mechanism is NOT established and this issue does not claim one.** It is filed because a verdict that disagrees with its own log is the exact class of thing the sealed-gate design exists to make impossible, and because a note in a session log would be lost.

## It failed in the SAFE direction, which is why this is severity low

The seal refused to claim green for a run it could not confirm had finished. That is the correct bias: the alternative failure -- a run that aborts and seals empty -- is the false green the whole mechanism is built to prevent. Nothing was mis-reported, and no work proceeded on a bad verdict.

What it cost was a few minutes of reading the `.out` to establish that the suite had in fact passed. What it would cost at a worse moment is trust in the seal, which is expensive in a project whose first rule is to read seals rather than exit codes.

## What is known

- The project was Prolix, gates green, mid-session on 2026-08-10.
- The command was `bin/prolix test mix`, invoked from a non-interactive shell with stdout and stderr redirected to a file.
- The seal was read in the SAME shell invocation as the command that wrote it, immediately after it returned -- `bin/prolix test mix > log 2>&1; wc -c < tmp/test/LATEST_MIX.errors`.
- No other `bin/prolix` process was believed to be running. A `mix credo` had run earlier in the session, but not concurrently.
- `LATEST_MIX.out` was the completed log of the run in question, not a stale one.

## What is NOT known

Whether the sentinel was left by this run or by an earlier one whose symlink had not been replaced; whether reading `LATEST_*` immediately after the writing process exits is subject to a window where the symlink and its target disagree; or whether something in the redirected non-interactive invocation path differs from an interactive one.

**Nobody should fix this from the above.** The next step is reproduction, not a patch: run the gate in a loop in the same non-interactive, redirected form and watch for a completed `.out` beside a sentinel `.errors`.

## REPRODUCED 2026-08-24 (vc) -- the class, deterministically, by the documented route

This issue asked for reproduction before any patch. The route was already on record, in the comment `seal_disagreement_reason` carries in `lib/runlog`: `write_errors_file` TRUNCATES the seal whenever rc is 0, and when that truncation fails -- an unwritable seal, a vanished directory -- **it warns and returns 0**, so the seal keeps the in-flight marker `open_run_log` seeded.

Driven directly, with the seal made unwritable between seeding and sealing:

    seeded .errors:  run in flight (or aborted before sealing) -- no completed verdict...
    (run completes, exits 0)
    write_errors_file rc=0
    seal now:        run in flight (or aborted before sealing) -- no completed verdict...
    seal bytes:      84            (0 would mean GREEN)
    seal_is_inflight: YES

That is this issue's symptom exactly: a completed run whose verdict file says it never completed.

**IT IS NO LONGER SILENT, which is the substantive change since this was filed.** Two announcements now fire where the original observation had none:

- `write_errors_file` itself: `cannot seal <path> -- the run was GREEN but its seal could not be written`.
- `seal_disagreement_reason`, called from `print_run_verdict` on EVERY kept run: `returned 0 WITHOUT SEALING A VERDICT -- killed, timed out, or the seal could not be written`.

The second is the one that matters, and it reached this path deliberately. Its own comment names this issue: the ledger-based check in `run_all` only exists inside `<cmd> all`, and 0015's instance was a SINGLE GATE -- the path the ledger cannot see. It landed 2026-08-17 in the 0016 carry, a week after this was filed.

**The seal also fails SAFE here, and that was already true.** A non-empty `.errors` reads as FAILED to `[ -s ]`, so no consumer believes a green. What was missing was never safety; it was anyone being told which of two very different things had happened.

## What this does NOT establish

**That this was Prolix's cause.** The recorded evidence argues against it: an immediate re-run there sealed correctly, and an unwritable seal or a vanished directory would persist across a re-run. So the Prolix instance remains unexplained, and a transient cause -- something in the redirected non-interactive invocation, or a race this reproduction does not model -- is still open.

What has changed is that a recurrence is now announced rather than left for a reader to notice by comparing a log against its seal by hand. If it happens again, the run says so.

## Why it is worth keeping despite being unreproduced

The seal is the project's unit of truth. Every rule that follows from it -- read seals not exit codes, a missing seal is worse than an empty one, a determinate zero is legitimate but a silent zero is not -- assumes the seal and the run agree. This is one recorded instance where they did not, and one instance is enough to justify looking, even if it turns out to be an artefact of how the command was invoked rather than of how the seal is written.

## Resolutions

**CLOSED 2026-08-24 (vc). hv ruled: leave the exit status alone.**

The class is reproduced on demand (see above), and the state is now announced twice on every kept run where it was silent when this was filed. The seal itself has always failed SAFE -- a non-empty `.errors` reads as FAILED to the `[ -s ]` test every runner defines green by -- so nothing could believe a green; what was missing was anyone being told which of two very different things had happened, and that is what the 0016 carry added on 2026-08-17.

**The run still exits 0, deliberately.** Making an unsealable green run exit non-zero was weighed and refused: `print_run_verdict` annotates and never suppresses, and its own comment gives the reason -- a guard that quietly changes a verdict is a bypass wearing a safety label. The rc and the seal disagreeing is exactly the state `seal_disagreement_reason` exists to NAME, and naming it is the whole mechanism. Turning the annotation into a status change would remove the one place where both claims are in hand and compared.

**Closed on the reproduction, not on an explanation.** The Prolix instance's own cause remains unestablished, and the recorded evidence argues against the route reproduced here: an immediate re-run there sealed correctly, and an unwritable seal or a vanished directory would persist across one. If it recurs, it now says so, which is the condition under which this stops being an unreproduced note and becomes a diagnosis.
